name: Paris Basin
tagline: Nuclear-heavy grid, close to millions of users.
context: Your electricity is already low-carbon, so renewables add little here. Your real levers are efficiency, hardware lifespan, and how much you choose to grow.
source: Grid intensity: order of magnitude from RTE 'Bilan électrique' (France ~20-60 gCO2e/kWh in recent years). Prices and demand: game design.

name: Nordic Fjord
tagline: Cold air, hydro power, far from users.
context: Free cooling and clean hydro make this the easy place to be green. But you are far from your clients: they pay less and arrive slower.
source: Hydro-dominated Nordic grids are typically well under 50 gCO2e/kWh (order of magnitude). Prices and demand: game design.

name: Coal Valley
tagline: Cheap land, hungry clients, a coal-heavy grid.
context: Every kWh you draw here emits more than ten times what it would on a nuclear or hydro grid. Clean power contracts are your biggest lever, and carbon prices hurt the most.
source: Coal-dominated grids are typically 600-800 gCO2e/kWh (order of magnitude, e.g. Ember country data). Prices and demand: game design.

name: Sun Belt
tagline: Endless sun, tax breaks, and not much water.
context: Solar is cheap and growth is fast, but it is hot and dry. Evaporative cooling saves energy by drinking water that farms and towns also need.
source: Hot, dry sites rely more on evaporative cooling (higher WUE). Gas-heavy grids are roughly 350-450 gCO2e/kWh (order of magnitude). Prices and demand: game design.
